en: Udāna 6.9 Upātidhāvantisutta Thus have I heard:
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the Blessed One was sitting in the open air during the pitch-black darkness of night while oil lamps were burning.
At that time, many moths were falling repeatedly into those oil lamps, meeting with misfortune, meeting with disaster, and meeting with misfortune and disaster.
The Blessed One saw those many moths falling headlong into those oil-lamps, meeting with misfortune, meeting with disaster, meeting with misfortune and disaster.
Then the Blessed One, having understood this matter, on that occasion uttered this inspired utterance:
“They rush headlong; they do not heed the essence.”
like moths falling into a flame,
some remain fixed upon what is seen and heard.
